transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, yes, thank you. Um, well, I suppose I should start by giving you a little context. I’m a graphic designer, and I’ve been doing this for a long time—ever since I got my bachelor's degree, really. So I know my job, and I know I'm good at it. Our work is incredibly detail-oriented, dealing with pixels and bleeds and typography, which is fine, I actually love that part of it. But I came in today because lately... well, I just keep getting these incredibly nagging thoughts that are driving me up the wall. 

It’s like my brain just gets stuck. I’ll finish a project, and I'll just be hit with this intense, lingering thought that I’ve missed some tiny mistake in a layout. Like a microscopic alignment issue or a typo that no one else would ever notice, but it feels catastrophic to me. Or—and this is the one that really gets under my skin—I'll start worrying that I’ve sent the wrong version of a file to a client. You know how it is with digital files, you have version one, version two, the final version, the *actual* final version. And I just get terrified that I attached the wrong draft to the email. 

And the most frustrating part of the whole thing is that even when I can see that it’s probably fine, and the rational, professional part of my brain is telling me, "You did this correctly, you always do," my mind just keeps circling back to it. It just loops and loops. I'll be trying to eat dinner or start a new project, and my brain is just pulling me right back to that one specific email or that one specific layout, wondering if I messed it all up. It's just so exhausting to deal with.
When these thoughts come up, do you find yourself doing anything specific—like checking the file multiple times or going back to emails repeatedly—to make sure everything is correct?

Yes, exactly. I mean, it’s almost embarrassing to admit how much I do exactly that. It’s not like I’m spending, you know, twelve hours a day doing it—I’m still getting my work done, it hasn't completely taken over my entire day or anything. But before I submit any work now, I have this whole... process, I guess you'd call it. 

I’ll go to hit 'send' on the email, and then I just freeze. I have to minimize the email, go back into Illustrator or InDesign, and re-open the file. And then I’ll sit there and literally compare all the layers. Like, I’ll toggle the visibility on and off just to make absolutely sure I didn't accidentally hide a text layer or leave a sketch layer visible in the background. And then, of course, I have to re-save it. But even after I save it, I’ll sit there and sometimes mentally walk through every single design choice I made one more time. Like, 'Okay, the kerning on the header is correct, the bleed is an eighth of an inch, the color profile is CMYK...' just reciting it all to myself to prove I did it right. 

And I know it sounds a bit ridiculous, and like I said, I still get everything turned in, but it just makes me so much slower. I used to just design and feel this great sense of flow, but now I feel so much less free creatively. The whole time I’m working now, I’m just anticipating this tedious checking routine I know I'm going to have to do at the end. It just completely drains the joy out of the actual art of it, you know? Because instead of thinking about the visual balance or the emotional impact of a piece, I'm just bracing myself for having to re-open the file and check the layers again. It just drags the whole day down.
